name: British Columbia: public health coverage for newcomers
name_fr: Colombie-Britannique : assurance maladie publique pour les nouveaux arrivants
description: Who is covered by Medical Services Plan (MSP) by immigration status, any waiting period for newcomers, how to apply, the public drug-coverage model and the share of adults with a regular health care provider.

attributes.legal_status: in force (eligibility rules as published on the access date)

eligibility_by_status.citizen: Eligible as a resident (residency and presence rules apply).
eligibility_by_status.permanent_resident: Eligible (citizens and permanent residents living in B.C. and present at least six months in a calendar year).
eligibility_by_status.work_permit_holder: Some holders of work permits valid for six months or more may be deemed residents.
eligibility_by_status.study_permit_holder: Some holders of study permits valid for six months or more may be deemed residents.
eligibility_by_status.visitor: Not eligible (visitors and tourists are excluded from every provincial plan reviewed).

attributes.status_dependency: Which rule applies depends on the user's immigration status, which is unknown (USER-PROFILE.md: 'Citizenship(s) and current country of residence', 'Existing Canadian status or application').

newcomer_waiting_period.arriving_from_outside_canada: Wait period = the rest of the month in which residency begins plus two further months; applies to new and returning residents (one gov.bc.ca page says the wait is waived for returning Canadians, permanent residents and CUAET arrivals — conflicting; verify with Health Insurance BC).
newcomer_waiting_period.moving_from_another_province: Same wait period; keep the former province's coverage meanwhile.

attributes.how_to_apply: Online, in person or by mail (gov.bc.ca/MSP/applyforhealthcare); apply immediately after arrival.
attributes.drug_coverage_model: Fair PharmaCare: income-based annual deductible, then the plan pays part of eligible costs (PMPRB 2020/21 summary); B.C. also has a national-pharmacare agreement covering listed contraception and diabetes medications (Health Canada, 2026).

regular_provider.source: CIHI indicator 'Canadians With a Primary Health Care Provider', Statistics Canada CCHS

sources.methodology: Weighted percent of adults 18+ reporting a regular/primary health care provider (family doctor, nurse practitioner or other); 95% confidence interval given. 2025 adult questions were harmonized, so compare with earlier years with caution.

verification.notes: Provincial page(s) fetched directly where status is 'verified'; otherwise some content came from search-engine extracts of official pages (403 or bot-check on fetch). Regular-provider figures parsed from CIHI's published data table.

limitations: Eligibility text summarises official pages and is not legal advice; temporary-status rules change often. Drug-plan designs are from PMPRB's 2020/21 summary and may be out of date. 'Without a regular provider' is 100 minus the CIHI share (simple arithmetic).
